meaning_by_symbol.BS: wobble or bulge plus muffled sound
meaning_by_symbol.HS: clashing tones plus 2 configurations plus shimmering edges
meaning_by_symbol.ES: too bright plus layered hum plus frozen or unresponsive faces
meaning_by_symbol.HI: blazing white plus harsh buzz plus hot faces
meaning_by_symbol.DE: drifting light plus blurred edges plus wavering pitch
meaning_by_symbol.CD: 1-2 bright corners plus clicking or ticking plus corner heat
meaning_by_symbol.PS: dim frozen plus silent plus cold or unresponsive
meaning_by_symbol.AC: random patch flicker plus broken start-stop hum plus edges normal
meaning_by_symbol.TB: hot all over but dim plus low rumble plus rough or gritty red
meaning_by_symbol.LI: dim or faint plus whisper hum plus washed-out patterns
meaning_by_symbol.1L: one-lamp direct or spill geometry: place lamp close to the target-bright face so the opposite target gets only spill; hold fixed

reply.rationale: No defensible compositional paradigm is supported by this codebook. Although some symbols share characters (e.g. several end in S/C/I), there is no evidence of a stable substitution frame with recurring forms making the same meaning contribution across multiple entries. The meanings of whole codes are heterogeneous and not predictably compositional from any proposed subparts. In particular, pairs like RC/AC/CD do not show a consistent final C meaning, and PS/ES/HS/BS do not show a consistent final S meaning. The initial digit in 1L also fails the opaque index test: there is no paradigm showing 1 as a literal count morpheme alternating with other count values in the same frame. Therefore the safest analysis is a flat lexicon with all symbols treated as opaque lexical items.
